Episode 247. Liberation War of Lafrarosa (19)
"Ha, haa...!"
Thud!
Luna slumped to the ground, leaning against the wall. In front of her, only the upper half of Shimat remained, twitching on the floor.
How many hours had they been fighting?
After gaining the crimson energy, Luna completely lost her sense of time, dedicating herself to the fight. It was because Shimat clung to his thin thread of life until the very end.
Shimat's rank of Genesis was no lie. In fact, he had awakened once, making Luna's victory a miracle, a phenomenon.
"It was a good match... Shimat."
Luna felt like she could collapse from exhaustion at any moment, but the crimson energy still hovered around the two.
Shimat's red energy wave could no longer be seen. He slowly blinked his eyes, staring into space.
Due to their battle, most of the internal mechanisms and armors were damaged, leaving the sky open.
No aerial fortresses, no red energy of their people, no spirit energy, no blue ripples of the Plutonian Domination Swords.
Just a clean sky, something they hadn't seen in a long time. The clear blue sky, as if the continual war and destruction were all a lie, dyed Shimat's pupils.
Just then, the sun passed over the collapsed ceiling of Kri. Sunbeams, entering through the cracks in the ceiling, shattered and bounced off Shimat's body.
It seemed ironic.
The sun had never disappeared from that spot. It was as if the Sun God was carelessly reminding them of this fact by dropping sunlight.
Step, step...
Footsteps were heard from somewhere. Shimat didn't have the strength to turn his head. It wasn't Luna's footsteps.
"You've worked hard, my disciple."
It was Eltiot. First, he checked on Luna's condition.
"Master."
"From now on, you are the greatest swordsman among those I've taught."
"Thank...”
"Shh! Keep quiet or your vital energy might get damaged. Don't move at all from that position. The medical team will arrive soon."
As Luna was about to nod, Eltiot shouted again.
"Don't move!"
Luna blinked her eyes as a response. Eltiot finally nodded, satisfied.
Then he turned to look at Shimat. Neither Luna nor Shimat could see what expression Eltiot was making.
It was fortunate for Eltiot.

There was no way to hide his complicated feelings. It was a joyous event that his disciple had defeated the Red Plutonian Battle God and grown, but he felt somewhat responsible for the tragic end 'Shimat' had met.
Once, Shimat was like Luna, a person Eltiot had engraved in his heart of light.
The guilt that he, as a master, couldn't prevent Shimat from becoming twisted, leading to this predetermined end, pierced his heart.
'Maybe I could have held him tighter, so he wouldn't lose his way... before he committed these unforgivable acts.'
In the dying Shimat, Eltiot saw the image of a time when Shimat was abandoned by his people and in despair.
'Or maybe it would have been better to let him die back then... then he would have only lost his life.'
Now Shimat will have to face eternal condemnation, having lost his people, life, and the values he believed in all his life.
He will wander in the collar of chaos, unable to escape until the end of this world. And the witch will never show mercy.
"...Red Plutonian Battle God, you've been terribly shattered."
Eltiot approached Shimat and bent down. The backlight still obscured his expression.
"Wind Emperor..."
"It's the moment when the long years of slaughter and madness have ended. Now, do you feel relieved?"
"I'm not afraid of the price."
"You foolish thing! You still haven't learned. Back then, you weren't afraid, you weren’t scared of anything in the world, so you returned to the Red Plutonian, betraying those who took you in."
"That was then. But now, I'm not saying I'm not afraid because... it's not that."
"Then why?"
"Because my people are there."
Shimat tried several more times to see Eltiot's face, but the backlight didn't fade. Finally, he gave up and closed his eyes, continuing the conversation.
"In the midst of chaos, I will bear the most pain as a deity. Be bold when it's time to take responsibility. Isn't that what you said?"
Things have changed.
But now it was too late. Eltiot couldn't decide what to say to his old disciple who had finally realized his sins.
There had been too many events.
There had been too many deaths. The Plutonian people who had died betrayed by him still seemed to cry out in his heart of light.
But it was too late to resolve that resentment; a terrible fate was already waiting for Shimat. Shimat had nowhere left to fall.
"I cannot betray you and the Plutonian again, like I did before. If I am afraid, it's of betraying my people."
"Yes... We can't offer you a ritual in our way. Someday, in the distant future, if the day comes when you are released from these sins. I hope we don't meet like this again."
As if shaking something off, Eltiot stood up. Turning to go back to Luna, he heard Shimat's last words.
"It's not your fault, old man. I was the demon."
When Eltiot turned back, Shimat was no longer visible. He had already disappeared without a trace.
Eltiot couldn't take his eyes off the spot for a long time. It was as if he could still hear his screams.
"Such a cruel guy until the end."
Luna unwittingly said that, then glanced at Eltiot, fearing he might scold her for speaking.
Eltiot quietly stroked Luna's head.
"You have defeated such a strong and cruel man. My disciple, but it seems you take your master's words too lightly. If your vital energy is hurt, it's again my role to correct and heal it, isn’t it?"
The outside was getting noisy.
Comrades, and the medical team of Tikan and the priests of the Holy Kingdom, were descending from the golden ship. Saint Queen Lani was the first to find Luna.
"It's always so miraculous. Whenever I treat the Runcandel knights, they're always on the brink of death. As if no one but me can save them."
As soon as Lani used her divine power, Luna quickly felt better. She gestured to Eltiot several times, asking if she could speak now. Eltiot nodded.
"Thank you, Your Majesty, the Saint King."
"It's somewhat fortunate that not many people are injured since we deployed fewer personnel. Those Plutonian people insist that such wounds can be left alone, which is a bit of a problem."
Outside of Kri, the four Battle Kings were arguing with the priests. Lani shook her head, watching the scene.
"Anyway, you've fought a tough battle. On behalf of the Holy Kingdom, I must thank you once again. Now... we just need Jin Runcandel and Lord Murakan to return safely."
The passage to Lafrarosa was still open.

The golden ship and some comrades were spreading a protective barrier nearby, preparing for any possible rift impacts. And since Kinzelo or Zipple could suddenly come to the desert, the Vamel Alliance still couldn't relax.

It was almost twelve hours since the liberation device had arrived in Lafrarosa. Taking the margin of error into account, Jin and Murakan, along with the Plutonian people, should appear in the desert within the next 30 minutes.
"Emergency treatment is finished. Proper treatment should be done in Tikan or the Holy Kingdom, so let's move to the golden ship for now. Lord Immortal!"
"Huh? Now you too are calling me Lord Immortal?"
"Everyone in the alliance is calling you that. Maybe even the whole world? Just accept it, and please bring Luna and Eltiot to the golden ship."
Bale gritted his teeth and took the two to the golden ship.
Luna couldn't bring herself to go to the ship's infirmary and stood on the bridge, looking at the rift. The giant rift filled the entire front window of the bridge.
All her comrades couldn't hide their worried expressions. Kasimir and Jet were almost biting their nails, and Sandra seemed ready to throw herself into the rift as soon as someone opened the bridge.
Valeria was outside the bridge, tracking records. Blue windows typical of record magic floated near Valeria at the bow of the ship.
'Jin, please come back safely...!'
Frustrating sentences were written in the record windows. Amidst lines like "Jin Runeandel and Murakan are swept away by the dimensional storm," Valeria's heart burns.
Suddenly, a new sentence appeared in the record window.
"Lafrarosa is freed from its long curse."
Valeria's eyes widened. Many sentences in the record window began to light up, all related to the liberation of Lafrarosa.
Amidst her wildly beating heart, one unfamiliar sentence caught Valeria's eye.
"Your Jin Runcandel has succeeded."
It was a colloquial expression rarely used in record magic. Valeria didn't have time to ponder the reason, as a giant warm wind suddenly rose from below the golden ship.
As the dimensional gate in front of the ship closed, a new dimensional gate began to open on the desert's surface.

It was like the sea suddenly parting, the huge dimensional gate rippling. The members of the alliance on the ground were terrified of falling in, but the gate, like the final stage of a Plutonian Domination Sword, just splashed and didn't swallow people.
There was nowhere to escape anyway. It was a scale far beyond even the hull of the aerial fortress Kri. Valeria and her comrades, with trembling hearts, stared at the dimensional gate.
After a while, they could see it.
Lafrarosa emerging above the dimensional gate.
"This, is this really Lafrarosa!?"
The alliance members shouted. And tears continuously flowed from the eyes of the four Battle Kings.
"Lafrarosa... our land. Our world...!"
Lafrarosa quickly settled above the desert.
As if it had never disappeared, as if it had always been there.
